channel.title: New Indie Friday
channel.description: New independent music — indie, alt and surf rock with an Australian and New Zealand focus — curated weekly by Kim Rampling.

item.title: Making Hay - The Deliverables
item.description: A new Australian indie-rock project from Melbourne, Victoria, Australia fronted by Piers Buxton. This song is will part of their album release "Hop On It" on around October 29, 2026 (details from Bandcamp). Really great indie rock sound. And you just gotta love that voice!

item.title: Atomic Girl - Echomatica
item.description: Second song this week from Aotearoa (New Zealand), with this one Tāmaki Makaurau / Auckland based four-piece project/quartet Echomatica. A song to lose yourself in on a weekend going into autumn as the days shorten and life draws in. The YouTube video is very cool too.

item.title: Favourite Colours - InDuna
item.description: Give this one the time it deserves, and after that breakout around 0.40 this it really takes off. As his Spotify profile says “InDuna is presented as an independent/self-taught Afro-pop artist and producer, with a distinctive South Africa–New Zealand cultural story rather than a generic pop positioning”. And Africa you hear straight off with those banking vocals, so much so suddenly you're back in Jo'burg. Check out 'Are You in Love' and 'Say What You Want'.

item.title: Gold - Harley
item.description: This song came in late to the weekly updates due to dumb AI agent search issues, OK not that late as the EP was released on September 18, 2026. Cool song, with very much the Queensland Indie Rock sound. Really? Is that a thing? Whatever, that's what I think. It's a nicely complex composition, with break outs that take by surprise, and then fly up and away. If you want blues, listen to 'Take Me To The City' from the same EP, a whole different song type. These guys sure got depth!

item.title: walton vale - The Cheap Thrills
item.description: This group from Liverpool - hard not to recognise the accent even from Europe - was actaully formed back in 2010. If your check out their Spotify discography page: scroll down after the all prevailing Spotify ‘popular releases’, then —>(highlight) Singles and EP’s —>then click ‘Show all’. It then becomes clear that even if this is their first ‘album’, they have been releasing singles and EP’s since 2013. Moving on. One of those you listen to with the lyrics taking you through the all the crap we do to oursleves, only we just keep doing it. Wrapped up in a song that is sort of light and heavy at the same time. Like listening to life.

item.title: Martini Me Fatso - Matt Berninger
item.description: I first came across this song in late July this year, where it had been discovered via the then new AI Music Release Agent, with a title like that it’s hard to forget. For reasons I do not recall, it did not make the cut, and was not included as a ‘Release’ at the time, but hey, we can all change our minds, right? On (this) second listen, I have to admit it’s a great Indie Rock song, even if the ‘break’ around 1.44 in needs a little getting used to. Matt Berninger is primarily known as the frontman and lyricist of indie rock band The National, the American rock band from Cincinnati, Ohio, formed in Brooklyn, New York City, way back in 1999. Like a lot of things music American, even groups like The National get lost in World Music noise. I only really caught up with them with ‘Tropic Morning News’ from the album "First Two Pages of Frankenstein" released on April 28, 2023, which I did feature on the old Streamusique blog at the time. And why the gap between the ‘discovery’ in July and ‘release’ last Friday? That’s the new done thing: pre-release a single very early, then include it in the next new EP or album. So what do I know about music marketing?! Great song!

item.title: Grace - The Halves
item.description: Great Indie Rock song from these guys from Melbourne, Australia. Check out ‘Trackstar’ and ‘Cold in Gloom’ from the same Optus EP, hell forgot that, check out the whole EP!

item.title: Who's That. - The War on Drugs.
item.description: Latest new release. It’s been a while, and was getting to missing them. Classic Drugs song, and clasic Adam Granduciel composition. His guitar work is just a fresh as ever. And here’s the YouTube video Who’s That - watch him play.

item.title: Earth's Still Spinning - Ups and Downs
item.description: These guys have been around since 1993, after forming Brisbane, then moving to Sydney. Before my Australian time, and did not come across them when I was there, but hey that’s music discovery for you. As far as I can tell, this is just there forth album, or rather EP, and it’s been a while since The Sky's in Love With You back back in 2017. This is a great laid back song, one to listen in those relective moments we all have.

item.title: I Turn - Darren Middleton
item.description: Classic indie rock song from the latest album from Darren Middleton. Surprisngly his 6th solo album - was the whole Powderfinger thing that long ago? Yes, it was and he’s forever noted as ‘as guitarist and songwriter’ for that great Australian band (1991 - 2010).

item.title: I Could Be Wrong - Linda Lindas
item.description: One thing did come out of death of everynoise.com was wider and wider search to find an alternative. And just to be clear, there really isn't one. Before turning to AI generated new music release search bots, one site I have used for many years is AllMusic that has a new release section which you can sign up for a weekly email. Long story short: The Linda Lindas new album, Gotta Get Out, was featured in this week's AllMusic, and this is my choice from that album. A very interesting LA based 'post punk, garage rock, power pop, new wave and rock en español' (from their Spotify blurb). Reminds me in some ways of the British group 'Dream Wife', even if that group does have a male drummer.

item.title: Ronalina - Remi Miles
item.description: A late summer, where did that girl go who you met on holiday, and why did you not stay in touch with her, type of song.

item.title: The Way It Goes - World News
item.description: Yet another great song from the London band - which I have just added to a Spotify Playlist - World News (the best of).

item.title: Rock and Roll - Bilk
item.description: Always liked this group, and happy to see they are slowly coming back. What I mean by that is there was there was a sort of ‘gap’ between the release of the album “Essex, Drugs, and Rock and Roll” in January 2025, and the single “Do Ya Want It” in June 2026. And, yes, that’s a bit of a gap, as the English would say. With this one they seem to be moving in, maybe could call it a curved direction. Sure this it sounds like (don’t say it), only it does stand as a great rock song all by itself.

item.title: Gotta Go - Calico City
item.description: Great song from these guys from Perth, Western Australia, love the mixture of rock and reggae - it’s impressive. Check out thier other singles: Ghost, from December 2025, and Back in the Before from February this year - wow guitar! ABC Australia’s Unearthed, as more details here. Really looking forward to the release of their debut EP in September. Another Perth based group via the new-release-agent

item.title: Fun - The Big Moon
item.description: A very summer song, one to listen to out of the heat. The Big Moon are a British indie-rock four-piece from London, that formed in 2014. I first came across them in 2022, with ‘Trouble’, which I first heard as a single and which was then included in the album “Here is Everything”, released in October of the same year. Great music.

item.title: Bullet Train - DICE
item.description: My selection from their newly released album ‘I Thought The Altitude Would Make It Worth The View’. DICE are indie rock group from Perth, Western Australia, with this being their second album after ‘Midnight Zoo’ from August 2024. Another group I had yet to come across, and that was pulled out by the music release agent. More great Surf Rock.

item.title: Kick in the Shins - Radio Free Alice
item.description: Sometimes the new-release-agent only throws up songs at a later date, and in the case of this one, nearly 3 weeks after. Which is fine, as do we care if it’s late! I missed out on their EP ‘Radio Free Alice’ back in November 2023, because, why? Not sure. Let’s just blame it on Spotify. These guys are everything you want to hear from an Australian indie-rock band. And they are do a Euro tour

item.title: Let Me Burn - Kyla-Belle
item.description: Not being a huge fan of country music, Australian or otherwise, I would have passed on the artist. Only this song is “the song is a step into a new era of her career" and in her words "influenced by a different perspective towards music". As a contrast, listen to her ‘Took A Turn’, song with the rapper Nooky

item.title: Dashboard Light - Work Drugs
item.description: More summer music. Although not typical Indie music, I have been following this group since I first came across 'Flaunt the Imperfection' from their album of the same name released back in August 2017. It's dreamy music, and this new release is suited for hot summer evenings sitting around on the beach watching the sun go down. A chill, and relax song. Work Drugs are from Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA and the why for in the name can be found here in Wikipedia - it's not what you think.

item.title: What's The Worst That Can Happen? - The Lilacs
item.description: Confess I had not come across this band from Wigan, near Manchester before, although they have been around since 2018. This is a great song for the summer, taking everyone away from all the usual doom and gloom (and heat!), off on your summer holiday road trip to where you always dreamed to go. Catchy uplifting tune. And the old man on the bus is all too right.

item.title: Bitter - Mackenna Rose
item.description: an artist from the Gold Coast no less, where I had the pleasure of living and working for five years. Even if Mackenna Rose talks in the plural in here’ About the artist’ Spotify description, I have not yet discovered any other songs by her. A song that grows with each listen

item.title: Covered In You - The Rolling Stones
item.description: No point at all in going into much of anything about them - we all know! Out of the 14 songs on this album, this one just appeals. It swings between the old Stones and something new, to the extent that Mick’s voice changes with sections. Sure, there’s bigger ‘tunes’ on this album. But I like this one. And yes it going to be one of their great albums!

item.title: Is This Real - overpass
item.description: From the album “Elsewhere, Always” released 5 June, 2026. First came across this Birmingham band back in 2021 with the release of ‘Otherside of Midnight’ in February that year, one of my favorite songs from that year. There have been been many more, with that clean, guitar Indie sound. This is one of those.

item.title: My Mind - Blush
item.description: This song has lots going for it, with a very cool medley section after a hard opening, that goes full grunge just after half way. I have only just discovered this group, and have featured them on my artist Spotlight page - read it here. Blush is one to watch out for, and really looking forward to more of their music.

item.title: Coal Dust - Rum Jungle
item.description: From their new album “Marginalia”, frankly a good, very typical Australian Indie song. "Rum Jungle is an Australian indie/alt-rock four-piece from Newcastle, New South Wales. They built their following on the local Newcastle scene before breaking through nationally." Also check out ‘Lowlife’, which for various complicated new site reasons, was my original pick from that album.

item.title: Heart Has To Work So Hard - Blondshell
item.description: Blondshell (real name Sabrina Teitelbaum) is originally from New York, USA, and is now based in Los Angeles, California, with music composed and written by herself. Such a great Indie Rock song, even if Spotify calls it bubblegrunge (eh?) Really like the driving beat, and the guitar backing and breakout is very cool.

item.title: A.D. - 32 Tens
item.description: Great song and stuff plus add to later. A single released on 15 May 2026. Been a while since I featured some bad arse rock music. Great indie rock song from this British group from the Northwestern UK town of Warrington. Get rockin', as they used to say.

item.title: Mamma Don't Cry - Joan & the Giants
item.description: Missed this one back two weeks ago at the end of April. I have listened to new releases before from this Melbourne based alt pop-rock band (whatever that means) only have never featured any of them. Don't be fooled by the long intro that sounds sort folksy as it is really not what the song is about. It takes nearly a minute (around 0.52) to hit its stride and become a great rock song.

item.title: Highwave - Moon Taxi
item.description: From their new album of the same name, released March 6, 2026. This is a very cool US indie rock song by this well established group that you probably have never heard of. First came across these guys back in 2018 with the release of their album “Let The Record Play”, where I see from Spotify I liked ‘Too High’, ‘Good As Gold’ and ‘No More Worry’, all from that same album. Three songs from one album is unusual for me, so I remember waiting in anticipation for the release of Moon Taxi’s next releases. Only to find myself skipping the “Silver Dream” album in 2021, and then liking ‘Set Yourself Free’ from the album of the same name, released in 2023 - still my favorite Moon Taxi. Moon Taxi are an indie/alt‑rock band from Nashville, Tennessee, in the USA and actually have been active since 2006. This is what used to be one of the joys of Spotify: discovering bands who are 'BIG' in the vast US market that you have never heard of. A discovery process that has got so much harder as Spotify continues to relentlessly push it's 'Made for (you)' and 'Discover Weekly' algorithm (now read AI) generated playlists. Bring back humans.
